source: 3-loop banana with 1 massive (msq) + 3 massless internal propagators — Phase 3 oracle for the mixed-mass axis (ROADMAP row 'all-massless / all-equal-mass → mixed: some massive, some massless').  Same 3-loop banana topology as banana_3loop but with only the first internal line carrying the W-like mass.  Exercises the AMFlow scaleless-sub-sector detection and mass-injection AMFMode under mixed-mass conditions at 3 loops — neither covered by existing benches (banana_3loop is all-equal-mass; tt_2loop_box is 2-loop mixed).  Target is the corner j[bn3mix, 1,1,1,1, 0,...] at psq = -3, msq = 1, eps = 1/1000.

cpp_sampled_status.result: completed and matches Mathematica reference at rel ≤ 2.88 × 10⁻³⁰ across all 5 sampled values (corner + 4 dotted masters).  First 3-loop mixed-mass oracle for the Phase 3 'some massive, some massless' axis.  No audit divergence surfaced — the AMFlow mass-injection mode (η on the single W-massive propagator) and scaleless-sub-sector detection under mixed-mass conditions both work correctly end-to-end.  All imag parts are at the numerical noise floor (10⁻⁸⁴ to 10⁻⁸⁷ absolute), matching MMA's noise floor at the same level — confirming the Euclidean-kinematics integral is real to printed precision.
cpp_sampled_status.note: All 5 sampled values pass at rel ≤ 2.88 × 10⁻³⁰.  C++ wallclock 56 s vs MMA 96 s — C++ ~1.7× faster.  MMA log shows 4-level subsystem recursion (3-loop top → 2/1-loop intermediates → vacuum ending).  Compare via tools/bench/compare_sampled.py.
